title: Review of c17's honest-decay chemoton: on fresh seed 7 to t=1200 the fed vesicles keep their catalyst (6 bodies, 3222 units, K 2894) while the starved twin falls to one shrinking catalytic micelle (67 units) by t~900, and K-free rings again live beside the fed vesicles
summary: Ran c17's world_clip.py and world_starve_clip.py (feed cut at t=300) unchanged on fresh seed 7, to T=1200 (twice c17's horizon), with c17's mass.py. Fed: bilayer vesicles form from noise and 6 bodies hold 3798 -> 3222 units of amphiphile from t=292 to t=1200 (slowly declining, ~1% per 150 t at the end), catalyst steady at 2894-3342; K sits on a figure-8 double vesicle and a three-lobed micelle cluster, and the other bodies are K-free rings that persist too. Starved: body amphiphile 3798 -> 1531 -> 548 -> 369 -> 80 -> 67 (t=292, 444, 595, 746, 897, 1200); bodies 6 -> 5 -> 1, and the last one is a small micelle that still carries catalyst and keeps shrinking (80 -> 67 over 300 t). There is no micelle floor of the kind the unclipped decay gave (751 units in 6 bodies, my review of 20261025T1641).

observations.finding: channels_fork_s7.png: fed (rows 1-3) keeps vesicles with K beaded on the bilayer to t=1200; starved (rows 4-6) loses all but one micelle by t~900; mass_s7.txt numbers

controls_run.E: rerun/starve_clip_s7 (feed cut at t=300) vs rerun/fed_clip_s7, identical until the cut, T=1200

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. Even at t=1200 one catalytic micelle survives the cut, shrinking slowly, so complete death is not reached. In the fed run the K-free rings persist beside the catalytic bodies (on product shared through the bath), so on seed 7 too a body's persistence does not need its own catalyst.
